question: Does rendering reviewed concealed-hand tile crops into a player-side meld visual domain improve SIFT transfer on reviewed regular exposed melds?
interpretation: The hand-to-meld domain transform shows a real positive signal on this small development batch.
The gain is strongest on the reviewed P-suit sequences after Mahjong-valid group decoding.
Simple perspective/blur synthesis plus SIFT is still not accurate enough to replace the real public_meld SIFT path.
The S/M failures repeatedly collapse toward a wrong triplet class, so the remaining bottleneck is identity representation/calibration rather than meld geometry alone.
Opponent top_group identity accuracy was not measured because this batch contains no reviewed opponent exposed-meld identity ground truth.
next_small_batch: Fuse real public_meld SIFT scores with synthetic hand-to-meld SIFT scores before introducing a learned classifier. Keep the legal three-tile group decoder and measure whether the synthetic branch adds value to the existing real-meld SIFT path.
